outlook.statement: Your Board of directors are continuously looking for new avenues for future growth of the Company.
The NBFC sector is poised for sustained growth, driven by rural and semi-urban credit demand, digitization, and financial inclusion initiatives.

The Company aims for steady growth in retail, SME, and structured finance; stronger risk management with 90-day NPA norm, provisioning, co-lending & investment limits; better governance & controls; technology adoption including digital lending and fintech integration with IT/cybersecurity focus; proportionate regulation under Scale-Based Regulation; and diversified funding to manage liquidity and ALM risks.
The management is confident of delivering stable and sustainable growth, aligned with its vision of inclusive financial empowerment.
Global NBFC sector valued at approximately USD 218.88 trillion in 2024, projected to reach USD 259.48 trillion by 2034, growing at a CAGR of around 2.15%.
Retail NBFC segment forecasted to increase revenue from USD 288.4 billion in 2024 to USD 492.5 billion by 2033, representing a CAGR of ~6.2%.
In India, NBFCs aggregate balance sheet expanded from ₹51.39 lakh crore in March 2024 to ₹61.09 lakh crore in March 2025, further increasing to ₹65.51 lakh crore by September 2025.
Total NBFC borrowings in India projected to reach $750 billion by FY27.
Commercial banking market size to grow from $4.39 trillion in 2025 to $5.03 trillion in 2026 at a CAGR of 14.5%.

litigation: ORDER RECEIVED FROM THE SECURITIES APPELLATE TRIBUNAL (SAT) DATED 29.04.2025 regarding alleged violations of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 1997 by promoter in 2007. SAT set aside direction at para 26 of WTM Order dated July 07, 2020 and remanded to SEBI for limited reconsideration; upheld all other findings including penalty order.

SEBI ORDER DATED 08.10.2025 (WTM/AN/IVD/ID5/31713/2025-26) against Mr. Rajiv Kotia (Promoter) and other entities: 1) Directive to divest excess shareholding (~1.54%) beyond 15% threshold and deposit proceeds in IPEF within three months. 2) Prohibition on certain family members from securities market participation for three months. 3) Requirement for compliance reporting to SEBI within two weeks after divestment. Promoter has complied with divestment, deposited proceeds in IPEF, and submitted compliance report.

The promoter has received order dated 29.04.2025 from SAT, wherein mentioned that: 3. There is no error apparent on the face of the record and therefore, the review application is rejected. However, in the unique facts and circumstances of this case and to give quietus to the matter, in our view, the matter may be remitted for limited purpose to reconsider the direction at para No. 26 of the WTM order 4. On our direction, learned counsel for the SEBI has taken instructions and submits that the direction at paragraph 26 of the WTM order dated July 07, 2020 may be set aside and the matter may be remanded to consider and pass appropriate direction. Applicant is agreeable to this suggestion. By consent of both parties, therefore, d) Directions at para 26 of the WTM Order dated July 07, 2020 are set aside and SEBI is directed to pass fresh directions after hearing both parties on that limited issue. e) All other findings in SAT Order dated August 24, 2022 and WTM Order dated July 07, 2020 stand confirmed. f) The AO Order dated May 18, 2020 is also upheld. 2. As prayed for by the learned counsel for the SEBI, it is clarified that this order will be not treated as precedent

After That, SEBI Order Dated 08.10.2025 Received in the matter of Sungold Capital Limited The SEBI issued final order of SEBI dated 08 October 2025 bearing reference WTM/AN/IVD/ID5/31713/2025‐26 has been issued against Mr. Rajiv Kotia (Promoter of the Company) and other entities. A copy of the said SEBI order was uploaded on the website of the Company. The Board noted the contents of the order, which includes following points, and discussed the implications for the Company. A summary of the reported salient features of the order was presented to the Board, as follows: 1. Directive to divest excess shareholding SEBI has directed Mr. Rajiv Kotia to sell the excess shares (approximately 1.54% shareholding in the Company) that exceed the permissible threshold (i.e., beyond 15%) and deposit the sale proceeds in the Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) within three months. 2. Prohibition on market participation by certain family members The order bars certain family members of Mr. Rajiv Kotia from participating in securities markets for a period of three months. 3. Requirement of compliance reporting Mr. Rajiv Kotia is required to submit a compliance report to SEBI within two weeks after completing the divestment. Mr. Rajiv Kotia has successfully divested the excess shareholding (approximately 1.54%) in compliance with the directions issued by SEBI within the prescribed timeline. The proceeds from such divestment have been duly deposited into the Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF), in accordance with the SEBI Order. Further, a compliance report confirming the completion of the aforesaid actions has been submitted to SEBI within the stipulated time frame.
